Context/Background:
Circular RNA (circRNA) is a class of noncoding RNA with regulatory potentials. Here, we identified circRMST as an exceptionally abundant circRNA predominantly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with strong conservation between humans and mice.

To explore the functional role of circRMST, we designed two shRNAs targeting the backspliced junction (BSJ), achieving 70%–93% knockdown efficiency. In 3D Matrigel-embedded cultures, circRMST knockdown significantly impaired cell growth across three NEPC and four SCLC-A models. Additionally, cell cycle analysis in SHP77 cells revealed cell-cycle arrest. In vivo, SHP77 xenografts in NSG immunodeficient mice exhibited markedly reduced tumor growth upon circRMST depletion.
Prompt:
To investigate transcriptional changes following circRMST knockdown, we performed RNA-seq in SHP77 cells and identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes.

What are the most relevant pathways in a GSEA results with the differential gene list?  Nominate a target most relevant for neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
To dissect circRMST’s role in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC), we performed RNA-seq in the SHP77 small-cell/lung NE model after two independent shRNAs targeting the circRNA back-splice junction. Knockdown (70–93% efficiency) induced cell‐cycle arrest in SHP77 (not specified: replicates), yielding ~8,000–9,000 DE genes per shRNA (padj < 0.05). We jointly ranked genes by mean log2FC across shRNAs to run GSEA (preranked) against KEGG, GO_BP, Reactome and MSigDB Hallmark libraries.  

Step 0) Keywords & Candidate Genes  
Keywords: neuroendocrine differentiation; cell cycle arrest; GPCR signaling; ER stress; lysosome  
Candidate Genes: ASCL1; CGA; SSTR2; DDIT3; CDKN1A  

Step 0b) Dataset interrogation (joined mean log2FC)  
• ASCL1 (mean_lfc = –2.65), CGA (–3.39) confirmed downregulated.  
• SSTR2 (mean_lfc ≈ –2.20), CDKN1A (not detected; not specified), DDIT3 (not detected; not specified) were searched but below DE cutoff.  

Pathway Enrichments (GSEA preranked)  
counts_by_database:  
• KEGG_2016: 14 up / 8 down (64% up, 36% down, ratio 1.75)  
• GO_BP_2023: 284 up / 101 down (74% up, 26% down, ratio 2.81)  
• Reactome_2024: 155 up / 45 down (78% up, 22% down, ratio 3.44)  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 10 up / 1 down (91% up, 9% down, ratio 10.0)

Analysis  
GSEA highlights a dual program: upregulation of ER stress/lysosomal and cell‐cycle‐regulatory modules (mTORC1, mitotic spindle, UPR), and downregulation of neuroendocrine-lineage-defining GPCR networks (neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction, GPCR downstream signaling). The prominence of GPCR modules especially implicates neuroendocrine-specific receptors.  

Target nomination for NEPC  
SSTR2 (somatostatin receptor 2) is a canonical NE marker, is among the leading-edge members of the most suppressed “Neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction” pathway, and is clinically actionable via somatostatin analogs and radioligand therapy in neuroendocrine tumors. Its downregulation upon circRMST depletion suggests functional linkage and therapeutic potential in NEPC.  

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate SSTR2 expression and function in multiple NEPC models (IHC, ligand binding).  
2. Test whether circRMST directly regulates SSTR2 transcript or stability (RNA pull-down).  
3. Assess combination of circRMST knockdown with somatostatin analog treatment in xenografts.  
4. Confirm ER stress signature by measuring UPR markers (e.g., DDIT3, HSPA5).
